data.hypothesis: Increasing the tile from 2048 to 4096 lets the single-CTA path cover inputs through 4096 and halves the partial count for larger inputs. This may reduce launch and finalization overhead, but the larger per-CTA workload and smaller first-pass grid could reduce parallel efficiency, especially for large inputs. The experiment tests that tradeoff against the valid 2048-tile parent; no speedup is assumed.
data.notes: The selected parent was correct on 10 cases and measured 8.036 μs mean over three repeats; the baseline was correct and measured 46.244 μs mean over three repeats. These are prior controller measurements, not results for this candidate. The proposed change retains 128-thread CTA reductions, 64-bit accumulation, bounded tails, initialized partials, ABI, and default-stream ordering. The controller must validate correctness and measure repeated full-program timings before drawing a performance conclusion.
transformations: Increase kTileSize from 2048 to 4096. This also extends the one-CTA path to inputs up to 4096 elements.
For larger inputs, retain the two-pass hierarchy and one-CTA finalizer, reducing the first-pass partial count to ceil(n/4096).
Keep the 128-thread shared-memory CTA reduction and 64-bit local, partial, and final sums; each first-pass CTA writes its bounded tile result before the finalizer reads it.
